q: How do I fill the BRSR water discharge table by destination and treatment level?
title: BRSR water discharge table, filled in
short: Principle 6 essential indicator 4 asks for discharge in kilolitres to surface water, groundwater, seawater, third parties and others, each split into no treatment and with treatment, naming the level. Add them for total discharge, which also gives consumption as withdrawal minus discharge.
audience: EHS and BRSR teams at listed companies and their plants

ul: Surface water: a river, drain or lake through your own outfall.
Sent to third parties: a common effluent treatment plant, a municipal sewer, or another company that takes your water.
Others: anything that fits none of these; say what it is.
p: Each row has two lines, no treatment and with treatment, and the second asks you to specify the level. A note asks whether an external agency assessed the figures.

SEBI's guidance note describes three. Primary removes solids that settle or float. Secondary removes what remains dissolved or suspended. Tertiary raises the water to a higher quality before discharge, for example removing heavy metals, nitrogen and phosphorus. Water clean enough to need no treatment can be reported as such, with an explanation.

ul: Flow meter logs at the ETP outlet and at each outfall.
CETP invoices or statements in kL.
Sewer connection records for domestic sewage.
Your consent to operate for the permitted limits; but report metered actuals, not the limit.
Effluent that gets primary treatment before going to the CETP is "with treatment, primary", not "no treatment".
A zero liquid discharge plant that still sends domestic sewage to a sewer has discharge to report.
Total discharge larger than withdrawal, which usually means a meter or unit error.
Zero liquid discharge is the next question, essential indicator 5, not this one.

example.title: Worked example: a plant that withdrew 60,000 kL
lines: (iv) Third parties, with treatment (primary), to the CETP: 30,000 kL
(iv) Third parties, no treatment, domestic sewage to the municipal sewer: 4,000 kL

senseible: Senseible's BRSR draft is built from the electricity bills and fuel invoices you upload, covering the energy and Scope 1 and 2 rows. The water table needs your meter logs and CETP records.
